[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Word Embeddings (Word2Vec, GloVe, FastText)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Word embeddings are dense, low-dimensional vector representations of words that capture semantic and syntactic meanings based on their contextual usage. Unlike sparse representations like One-Hot Encoding, embeddings allow machine learning models to understand relationships such as synonyms, analogies, and contextual proximity."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Word2Vec: CBOW and Skip-Gram"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Word2Vec, introduced by Google in 2013, relies on two primary architectures: Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW) and Skip-Gram. CBOW predicts a target word from its surrounding context words, whereas Skip-Gram predicts the context words given a target word."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from gensim.models import Word2Vec
sentences = [['machine', 'learning', 'is', 'fascinating'], ['deep', 'learning', 'is', 'a', 'subset']]
model = Word2Vec(sentences, vector_size=100, window=5, min_count=1, workers=4)
vector = model.wv['learning']
print(vector)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. GloVe (Global Vectors for Word Representation)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Developed by Stanford, GloVe is an unsupervised learning algorithm that combines the advantages of global matrix factorization (like LSA) and local context window methods (like Word2Vec). It trains on a global word-word co-occurrence matrix, capturing semantic similarities more effectively over large corpora."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverages global statistical information directly."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Produces a symmetric co-occurrence matrix for vector training."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. FastText: Handling Out-of-Vocabulary Words"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Created by Facebook, FastText improves upon Word2Vec by treating each word as a bag of character n-grams. This allows the model to generate meaningful embeddings for out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words by summing the vectors of its constituent subwords."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"import gensim.downloader as api
fasttext_model = api.load('fasttext-wiki-news-subwords-300')
oov_vector = fasttext_model['unseenword']
print(oov_vector)"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":14,"paragraph":"Selecting the right embedding depends on your specific task. Word2Vec is fast and efficient for standard vocabularies, GloVe excels with global statistical patterns, and FastText is ideal for morphologically rich languages or datasets containing many rare and OOV words."}]
